payload.title: The Pigeon finds a hot dog!
payload.author: Mo Willems
payload.blurb: The Pigeon stumbles upon an unattended hot dog and can hardly believe his luck. Before he can take a bite, a very small duckling wanders over with a very large number of questions. The whole book unfolds as a conversation between the two, told in speech bubbles and simple line drawings. It runs short enough to read in a few minutes and works best out loud, with someone willing to do the voices.

payload.title: The Cruel Prince
payload.author: Holly Black
payload.blurb: Jude and her two sisters are taken to the High Court of Faerie as children, after the fae knight Madoc kills their parents and claims them as his own. Ten years on, Jude is seventeen and mortal in a world that treats humans as pets or amusements, and she wants a place at court badly enough to bleed for it. Standing in her way is Prince Cardan, the youngest son of the High King, who makes her humiliation something close to a hobby. The court runs on old rules about lying, debts, and hospitality, and Jude learns quickly that the rules are the only weapon a human gets.

payload.title: The Namesake
payload.author: Jhumpa Lahiri
payload.blurb: Ashoke and Ashima Ganguli leave Calcutta for a university town outside Boston, where they raise two children in a country whose customs never quite become their own. Their son carries the name Gogol, chosen under hospital pressure and tied to something in his father's past, and he spends much of his life resenting it. The novel follows the family across decades, moving between the parents' careful preservation of what they left behind and the children's easy, sometimes careless American lives. Lahiri writes in a quiet register, attentive to meals, houses, and the small negotiations that make up a marriage.

payload.title: A Stage Set for Villains
payload.author: Shannon J. Spann
payload.blurb: I don't know this book, and I'd rather say so than invent a premise for it.

payload.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
payload.author: Holly Jackson
payload.blurb: Five years ago, Andie Bell disappeared from a small English town, and her boyfriend Sal Singh was blamed and found dead soon after. Pip Fitz-Amobi, a sixth-form student with an appetite for research, chooses the case for her senior capstone project, convinced the accepted story has holes in it. She enlists Sal's younger brother Ravi to help her retrace the timeline, and the interviews turn up neighbours and classmates who would rather the questions stopped. The book is structured around Pip's project logs and transcripts alongside the narrative.

payload.title: Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone
payload.author: Benjamin Stevenson
payload.blurb: Ernest Cunningham narrates his own family's reunion at a snowbound resort in the Australian Alps, and he tells you up front that every member of the family has killed someone — including him. His brother Michael is out of prison, which is awkward, since Ernest is the one who put him there. Then a body turns up in the snow, and the gathering becomes something closer to a locked-room problem. Stevenson has Ernest narrate with constant reference to the old Golden Age rules of detective fiction, promising to play fair with the reader and then testing what fair means.

payload.title: Red Queen
payload.author: Victoria Aveyard
payload.blurb: In Mare Barrow's world, blood color decides everything: Silvers rule with superhuman abilities, and Reds like Mare scrape by as servants and soldiers. A pickpocket with no prospects, she lands a job at the Silver palace and then, in front of the entire court, does something a Red should not be able to do. The king's solution is to hide her in plain sight — passed off as a lost Silver noble and betrothed to a prince — while Mare quietly makes contact with a Red resistance movement. Aveyard writes a fast-moving court intrigue where the question is less what Mare can do than whom she can believe.

payload.title: The Secret Life of Bees
payload.author: Sue Monk Kidd
payload.blurb: Sue Monk Kidd's ravishing debut novel has stolen the hearts of reviewers and readers alike with its strong, assured voice. Set in South Carolina in 1964, The Secret Life of Bees tells the story of Lily Owens, whose life has been shaped around the blurred memory of the afternoon her mother was killed. When Lily's fierce-hearted "stand-in mother," Rosaleen, insults three of the town's fiercest racists, Lily decides they should both escape to Tiburon, South Carolina—a town that holds the secret to her mother's past. There they are taken in by an eccentric trio of black beekeeping sisters who introduce Lily to a mesmerizing world of bees, honey, and the Black Madonna who presides over their household. This is a remarkable story about divine female power and the transforming power of love—a story that women will share and pass on to their daughters for years to come.

payload.title: Mixing it
payload.author: Rosemary Hayes
payload.blurb: Fatimah is a devout Muslim. Steve has never given much thought to matters of faith. The two of them happen to be walking down the same street when a terrorist bomb explodes. Steve is badly injured, and when the emergency services arrive they find Fatimah cradling his head in her lap, talking to him, willing him to stay alive. But the media is there too, and the next day their picture appears in every newspaper. “Romeo and Juliet!” and “Love Across the Divide!” scream the headlines. Then the threats and anonymous phone calls start. Can the two young people rise above the hatred and learn to understand one another? And what about the terrorists, who surely aren't doing nothing as Steve and Fatimah try to break down barriers? Author Rosemary Hayes researched Islam's background and Muslim attitudes with a group of devout Muslim teenage girls in Cambridge, England, to give this story a sense of authenticity and reality missing from so much of the discourse on this heated topic.

payload.title: The Alchemist Graphic Novel
payload.author: Paulo Coelho
payload.blurb:
Paulo Coelho’s masterpiece tells the magical story of Santiago, an Andalusian shepherd boy who yearns to travel in search of a worldly treasure as extravagant as any ever found.

The story of the treasures Santiago finds along the way teaches us, as only a few stories can, about the essential wisdom of listening to our hearts, learning to read the omens strewn along life’s path, and, above all, following our dreams.

Acclaimed illustrator Daniel Sampere brings Paulo Coelho's classic to new life in this gorgeously illustrated graphic novel adaptation.

payload.title: The Outsiders
payload.author: S. E. Hinton
payload.blurb: No one ever said life was easy. But Ponyboy is pretty sure that he's got things figured out. He knows that he can count on his brothers, Darry and Sodapop. And he knows that he can count on his friends - true friends who would do anything for him, like Johnny and Two-Bit. And when it comes to the beating up on "greasers" like him and his friends - he knows that he can count on them for trouble. But one night someone takes things too far, and Ponyboy's world is turned upside down...

payload.title: That was then, this is now
payload.author: S. E. Hinton
payload.blurb: Continue celebrating 50 years of The Outsiders by reading this companion novel. That Was Then, This is Now is S. E. Hinton's moving portrait of the bond between best friends Bryon and Mark and the tensions that develop between them as they begin to grow up and grow apart.

payload.title: Once
payload.author: Morris Gleitzman
payload.blurb: Once by Morris Gleitzman is the story of a young Jewish boy who is determined to escape the orphanage he lives in to save his Jewish parents from the Nazis in the occupied Poland of the Second World War.

payload.title: Flowers for Algernon
payload.author: Daniel Keyes
payload.blurb:
Charlie Gordon is about to embark upon an unprecedented journey. Born with an unusually low IQ, he has been chosen as the perfect subject for an experimental surgery that researchers hope will increase his intelligence – a procedure that has already been highly successful when tested on a lab mouse named Algernon.

As the treatment takes effect, Charlie's intelligence expands until it surpasses that of the doctors who engineered his metamorphosis. The experiment appears to be a scientific breakthrough of paramount importance, until Algernon suddenly deteriorates. Will the same happen to Charlie?

payload.title: The Help
payload.author: Kathryn Stockett
payload.blurb:
Three ordinary women are about to take one extraordinary step.

Twenty-two-year-old Skeeter has just returned home after graduating from Ole Miss. She may have a degree, but it is 1962, Mississippi, and her mother will not be happy till Skeeter has a ring on her finger. Skeeter would normally find solace with her beloved maid Constantine, the woman who raised her, but Constantine has disappeared and no one will tell Skeeter where she has gone.

Aibileen is a black maid, a wise, regal woman raising her seventeenth white child. Something has shifted inside her after the loss of her own son, who died while his bosses looked the other way. She is devoted to the little girl she looks after, though she knows both their hearts may be broken.

Minny, Aibileen's best friend, is short, fat, and perhaps the sassiest woman in Mississippi. She can cook like nobody's business, but she can't mind her tongue, so she's lost yet another job. Minny finally finds a position working for someone too new to town to know her reputation. But her new boss has secrets of her own.

Seemingly as different from one another as can be, these women will nonetheless come together for a clandestine project that will put them all at risk. And why? Because they are suffocating within the lines that define their town and their times. And sometimes lines are made to be crossed.

In pitch-perfect voices, Kathryn Stockett creates three extraordinary women whose determination to start a movement of their own forever changes a town, and the way women, mothers, daughters, caregivers, friends, view one another. A deeply moving novel filled with poignancy, humor, and hope, The Help is a timeless and universal story about the lines we abide by, and the ones we don't.

payload.title: The First Stone
payload.author: Don Aker
payload.blurb: REEF IS AN EMBITTERED YOUNG OFFENDER, hardly able to contain his anger at the world over the death of his grandmother, the only person who had shown him any love. Seventeen-year-old Leeza is mourning the death of her older sister. A stone hurled in rage shatters both their lives and throws them together in the most unexpected way―and offers them a chance at healing.
